actions.reason: For long sequences (>=256 ids, at most 4 merges per id), apply_merges now uses a str-based path instead of the pure-Python heap. When every merge (p0,p1)->idx has distinct int idx with p0,p1 < idx <= 0x10FFFF, a pair of rank r can only be built from tokens < r. So the lowest-rank-first loop gives the same result as applying each merge once in rank order with str.replace on code points; replace matches left to right without overlap, exactly like merge(). The rank-ordered plan is cached against a snapshot copy of the merges, compared by dict equality. If the conditions do not hold, it falls back to the heap path. Equivalence harness: identical outputs. encode_ir 0.9870.
